justifications.clinical.clinicalOutcomes: Multiple RCTs show Cobb angle improvement with Schroth; effect sizes moderate. Long-term vs brace comparison ongoing.
justifications.clinical.efficiency: BSPTS or SOSORT-affiliated training; multi-day course; moderate cost.
justifications.clinical.caseloadApplicability: Applicable specifically to adolescent and adult scoliosis patients; very limited population scope.
justifications.clinical.reimbursement: Standard PT billing; no Schroth-specific code; commercial coverage for scoliosis PT varies.
justifications.clinical.marketDemand: Growing demand in scoliosis specialty clinics and pediatric ortho settings.
justifications.clinical.patientSatisfaction: Scoliosis patients value non-brace exercise alternatives.
justifications.business.cashPayViability: Scoliosis families actively seek Schroth and frequently pay cash when insurance won't cover the intensive 1:1 sessions required.
justifications.business.pricingLeverage: Rarity of certified providers in most US markets supports premium pricing well above standard PT rates.
justifications.business.marketDifferentiation: Few certified Schroth therapists per metro area; parents search by name for this method, creating real defensibility.
justifications.business.ownerLeverage: Other certified clinicians can deliver it, but the long certification pathway limits how quickly you can scale a team.
justifications.business.marketDemand: Strong within scoliosis niche and growing via parent networks, but invisible to the general consumer.
justifications.business.efficiency: Multi-course pathway (BSPTS/ISST) is expensive and time-intensive, with travel often required.
justifications.academicClinical.facultyRecognition: Recognized in pediatric/orthopedic niches but not a tenure-track credential; counts as continuing education more than scholarly credential.
justifications.academicClinical.scholarship: Modest but real literature base; certified clinicians do publish case series and trials on PSSE.
justifications.academicClinical.teachingValue: Useful for pediatric or spine modules in DPT curricula, particularly orthopedic electives.
justifications.academicClinical.evidenceDepth: Moderate; several RCTs and systematic reviews support PSSE/Schroth for AIS, though methodological limitations remain.
justifications.academicClinical.facultyDemand: Rarely listed as preferred in faculty postings; niche enough that programs don't require it.
justifications.academicClinical.efficiency: Significant time/cost investment relative to academic payoff.
